races.name: Total Task Consultancy Prosperity Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Shes Got The Blues
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back wins at 7f on good ground give her the strongest form profile in this field, and Myla Coppins retains a useful 3lb claim; she switches up to 1m but has run respectably at the trip, and six days since her last win means she arrives fresh and in form — her style at this track in a sprint finish suits the likely race shape best.

runners_data.name: My Old Mate
runners_data.note: Drops from softer ground where she has not performed well, and her 19-day absence with a note of fading in finishes is a concern in a race likely decided by a late sprint; Jude Fernandes (7lb claim) is inexperienced at this level, and her overall profile — zero wins and zero placed efforts in similar going — gives little confidence.

runners_data.name: Buckland Belle
runners_data.note: Carries a genuine hold-up style but her lone win came at 8f on good ground, so the trip and conditions are squarely in her favour; Conor Whiteley's 3lb claim is useful, and she is likely to try to position herself closer than her natural style dictates given the lack of pace — her style-fit in this shape is compromised but raw ability makes her a live threat.

runners_data.name: Labiche
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (p) and has been placed at 7f and 8f on softer surfaces, though her similar-going record of 1 from 6 is modest; Henry Candy has had no winners in the last 14 days from 12 runners, and the 25-day absence adds mild doubt — she will need to race out of her usual hold-up comfort zone and her style-fit score of 0.90 reflects that discount.

runners_data.name: She's Crafty
runners_data.note: Has a second at 7f on good ground in recent form and Alexandra Egan's 3lb claim helps offset her low OR of 52; George Margarson is also quiet in form (0 from 10 past 14 days), and 32 days since her last run is the longest freshen-up in the field — her natural instinct to sit deep means she must overcome a positional disadvantage in a race with no true pace.

runners_data.name: Lapidarist
runners_data.note: David Simcock's runner has the longest absence in the field at 95 days and the lowest official rating at 48, making her a speculative each-way play at best; her record shows consistency at 8f on standard ground but zero wins and no similar-going form of note, and Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim on a lightly-tried horse returning from a lengthy break is the most uncertain combination in the race.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field where every single participant carries a hold-up profile, this race at Windsor over a mile on good-to-firm turf is almost certain to be slowly and cautiously run, with the field drifting in a bunch before a sprint-finish develops in the straight. There is no horse to set a gallop, no forcing type to create gaps, and the apprentice/conditional jockey contingent adds further tactical uncertainty — expect a slow crawl through the early stages and a sharp, compressed finish where positioning at the two-furlong pole will be decisive. The race shape emphatically favours horses who can quicken from close to the pace rather than true deep closers, because in a muddling, slow-tempo race the back-markers will simply have too much ground to make up when the sprint ignites. Shes Got The Blues, My Old Mate, Buckland Belle, Labiche, She's Crafty, and Lapidarist are all hold-up types forced into a race with no natural leader — Shes Got The Blues, with her recent winning form and a degree of tactical versatility shown over 7f, is best placed to sit handily enough to capitalise, while Buckland Belle similarly has the raw ability to land close to the pace if her jockey acts early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Bunch
scenarios.trigger: If the field drifts through the early stages as a slow-moving pack and the race ignites with a sprint in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the field drifts through the early stages as a slow-moving pack and the race ignites with a sprint in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Bold Move Decides It
scenarios.trigger: If one jockey breaks from the pack mid-race to steal a lead and the field fails to respond quickly enough.
scenarios.body: If one jockey breaks from the pack mid-race to steal a lead and the field fails to respond quickly enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If a fast early tempo is somehow set and horses burn out, leaving genuine late runners to sweep past.
scenarios.body: If a fast early tempo is somehow set and horses burn out, leaving genuine late runners to sweep past.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Positional Chaos Rules
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of any natural leader creates a fractious, stop-start tempo with multiple false moves and rank outsiders catching the field flat-footed.
scenarios.body: If the lack of any natural leader creates a fractious, stop-start tempo with multiple false moves and rank outsiders catching the field flat-footed.

watchPoints.text: Shes Got The Blues is the most likely winner of this sprint-finish scenario and Myla Coppins must secure a position near the back of the leading group off the slow pace — watch whether she gets boxed in with six hold-up horses drifting.

Buckland Belle is flagged as racing out of her natural deep-closer role and Conor Whiteley may have to make a bold early move to secure a useful pitch — watch whether she gets shuffled back and loses her chance in the sprint.

Lapidarist returns after 95 days off for David Simcock and, while the trainer is capable of launching fresh horses, her modest rating and junior jockey combination with zero similar-going wins makes her a significant risk if tempo is genuinely slow.

My Old Mate's noted tendency to fade in finishes is directly problematic in a race almost certain to be decided by a sharp sprint over the final two furlongs — monitor how Jude Fernandes positions her in the early going.

With all six runners sharing the same hold-up profile, a pre-race draw/stall check is worth noting — any horse drawn widest who drifts further back at the start will lose valuable ground in a race where early positioning will be the key tactical variable.

races.name: Sporting Life Sri Lanka Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Seathegulls
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing two-year-old for Gary & Moore who finished fourth on Good last time; Rossa Ryan provides a strong booking and the 5f Good to Firm trip suits, making this a leading player in the tracking shape.

runners_data.name: Drum Major
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with consistent form figures of 679 on varied surfaces; Pierre-Louis Jamin takes the ride but the trainer's 0/10 14-day run rate tempers enthusiasm and the 40-day absence is a mild flag.

runners_data.name: Divine Whisper
runners_data.note: Ran second on Good over 5f on debut for Boughey and Loughnane — the form and conditions match precisely here; a strong booking and a horse with a proven placing on similar ground make this one of the more compelling profiles from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Blondie Larry
runners_data.note: Running style unclassified after a single run on Soft ground where she finished fifth; William Carver takes the ride for Jamie Osborne and the unknown quantity element is significant — she is lightly raced and the going change is an open question.

runners_data.name: Trust Yourself
runners_data.note: Two runs on Good over 6f have produced figures of 10th and 11th, and the switch back to 5f may help; however the flag for fading in finishes is a real concern in a race where the pace shape is unlikely to produce the ideal scenario for a horse who empties late.

runners_data.name: Wolf's Gallop
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and tempo-setter for Tom Lacey; the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 suggests this is his natural position, but the data cautions that his overall chance should be modestly tempered — he sets the shape rather than being the outright pace beneficiary, and his 5f Good form is moderate.

runners_data.name: Cash Flow Boy
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed debutant for Charlie Pike whose going record is unknown; Thomas Greatrex rides and the absence of any form data makes assessment near impossible — a pure wildcard in this field.

runners_data.name: Nascent Star
runners_data.note: Fourth on Soft debut for Hugo Palmer, who has a strong 14-day strike rate of 6/53; the step up to Good to Firm could unlock improvement and the unclassified running style means tactical flexibility, though lightly raced status adds uncertainty.

races.paceDynamic: Wolf's Gallop is the one confirmed front-runner in this 5f Windsor novice and, with no other genuine pace-pusher to challenge for the lead, Charles Bishop should have a straightforward time controlling the tempo from the gates. Seathegulls and Trust Yourself are both prominent-style types who will track closely behind, but neither has the profile to forcibly contest the lead, meaning Wolf's Gallop dictates an honest but not suicidal gallop on Good to Firm ground. Divine Whisper and Drum Major will be held up in rear, needing the pace to be sustained to the line to give them a chance of picking off tired rivals. With a single, uncontested front-runner likely to produce a regulated, even gallop on fast ground over the minimum trip, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-tracking horses who can sit just off the pace and produce a sharp finishing kick — pure hold-up types face too much ground to make up in only five furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wolf's Gallop Controls Clean
scenarios.trigger: If Wolf's Gallop breaks well and dictates an uncontested, measured gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: If Wolf's Gallop breaks well and dictates an uncontested, measured gallop throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Press Hard
scenarios.trigger: If Seathegulls or Trust Yourself disputes the lead vigorously and lifts the tempo above comfortable.
scenarios.body: If Seathegulls or Trust Yourself disputes the lead vigorously and lifts the tempo above comfortable.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and hold-up horses get a clear run into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong and hold-up horses get a clear run into the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Upsets The Form
scenarios.trigger: If Cash Flow Boy or Nascent Star produce a significantly above-par performance on debut or near-debut.
scenarios.body: If Cash Flow Boy or Nascent Star produce a significantly above-par performance on debut or near-debut.

watchPoints.text: Wolf's Gallop — if Charles Bishop gets a clean break and slots onto the rail, this horse could control the race entirely unchallenged, in which case the front-running position becomes far more advantageous than the STYLE_FIT discount implies.

Divine Whisper — Billy Loughnane must get a clean passage from a hold-up position over only 5f; any traffic problems in the short straight will leave too little time to recover, making draw and early positioning critical.

Trust Yourself — flagged for fading in finishes and yet to threaten in two runs on Good ground over 6f; if the pace is moderate the prominent horses sustain it to the line and this runner's tendency to weaken becomes decisive.

Cash Flow Boy — a completely unknown debutant in a race where pace shape is broadly settled; if Pike has been reporting strong home signals this could drift in-running before producing a late move worth monitoring.

Drum Major — 40-day absence combined with a trainer at 0/10 over 14 days is a dual negative flag; any market support in the ring for this hold-up type should be noted as potentially significant given the lack of obvious stable form.

races.name: Sri Lanka The Wonder Of Asia Handicap

runners_data.name: Angel Of Anfield
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner for Tom Clover with five runs over 5-7f on Good showing solid recent form (2-2-1-2); has sound similar-going record and takes up the lead comfortably here, though 50-day break and 3yo status at the top of the weights are mild queries.

runners_data.name: Combustion
runners_data.note: Chelsea Banham's five-year-old arrives on a hat-trick of wins over 5-6f on Standard but has very limited similar-going evidence (2 runs, no wins or places); a genuine prominent racer by nature, the sheer volume of pace in this field means he's unlikely to get his favoured spot, complicating his chance.

runners_data.name: Marcellinus
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's three-year-old is in strong form (3-2-1-2-2) and has thrived on Good ground, winning over this exact 6f course condition on his most recent run 12 days ago; sits neatly behind the leader in a prominent role and the quick return is a positive rather than a concern for this trainer.

runners_data.name: Alasrae
runners_data.note: George Boughey's three-year-old has been busy and consistent — won over 6f on Standard, placed on Good — but a 3-7-3 recent profile and a tongue-tie flag are mild negatives; Billy Loughnane rides and he handles all variants of Good ground though the big field at Windsor may test his positioning.

runners_data.name: Betsen
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old carries a 7lb claim with Myla Coppins and is in inconsistent form (4-7-0-9-1-8), winning last time on Soft over 5f; hold-up style needs a genuinely strong pace to fire on fast ground, and his similar-going stats (0W1P in 15) are a significant flag here.

runners_data.name: Desert Cop
runners_data.note: Ran just five days ago (finishing 7th over 5f Good) and George Baker's six-year-old has a solid similar-going record (14 runs, 3 places) but no wins on Good; races from hold-up and at 6f after a quick turnaround, the stamina question at this pace shape is less pressing than the lack of a win on this surface.

runners_data.name: Star Chorus
runners_data.note: Mike Murphy's four-year-old won over 6f on Standard and has placed over 5f in similar conditions; genuine hold-up runner who needs the pace to be honest enough to close, and his 21-day break is straightforward — the headgear flag (h) for hood may sharpen him, but Good ground stats (1W1P from 4) are respectable.

runners_data.name: Kiniro
runners_data.note: Dan Horsford's four-year-old is a natural hold-up horse but the congested rear of this field forces him into a more central map position he wouldn't naturally choose; returned with a second over 6f Soft 16 days ago following an absence, and the step up in pace from Standard to Good is untested (0W0P in 5 on similar going).

runners_data.name: An Outlaw's Grace
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old has won on Good going (2/6f/GOO) and shows solid similar-going form (1W3P from 8), but has posted three consecutive defeats; his true style is off the pace, and in a field this deep with hold-up types, being displaced to a midfield role he doesn't naturally occupy makes the tactical problem acute for Seamus Cronin (5lb claimer).

runners_data.name: Dublin Bay
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's three-year-old has won twice at 7f on Standard and finished 5th in a 6f Good field on his most recent run; races from hold-up and the step back to 6f may be on the sharp side, but two wins from six and a positive trainer record (2/21 over 14 days) give him live claims if the pace scenario opens up late.

runners_data.name: Jax Edge
runners_data.note: Won over 6f Good on his penultimate start and has a solid record in similar conditions (2W5P from 9); Gina Mangan rides for Christopher Mason who has been in decent form (2/7 T14), and at OR=78 as a prominent racer this horse is well-placed to take advantage of his natural style in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Supreme King
runners_data.note: David Evans's six-year-old is consistent over 5-6f but has zero wins or places from 15 runs on similar going, which is a serious flag on good-to-firm; Rossa Ryan takes the ride and the recent form string (1-5-3-5-5-1) shows ability but the going record makes a bold assessment difficult to justify.

races.paceDynamic: Angel Of Anfield is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger disputing the lead, is set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over six furlongs at Windsor. Marcellinus, Alasrae, Jax Edge, and Supreme King will press from prominent positions, creating a competitive but not scorching early tempo that keeps the field compressed rather than strung out. The genuine hold-up horses — Betsen, Desert Cop, Star Chorus, and Dublin Bay — will need the pace to honest enough to bring them into the closing stages, while Combustion, Kiniro, and An Outlaw's Grace are true prominent or hold-up types who have been pushed off their natural positions by the sheer volume of similar profiles in this field, making their task structurally harder. The race shape favours horses racing prominently in the slipstream of Angel Of Anfield — specifically those with the tactical speed to track a controlled pace and accelerate from 2f out on quick ground — as the single leader and manageable tempo means closers from deep will likely find insufficient cover is burned off ahead of them. This field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the race can naturally accommodate: Combustion, Kiniro, and An Outlaw's Grace are all unlikely to secure their preferred positions and must be assessed with that in mind, with Marcellinus, Alasrae, and Jax Edge best placed to hold the prime prominent ground behind the leader.

scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Of Anfield sets a controlled, uncontested lead and the prominent horses track smoothly before kicking from 2f out.
scenarios.body: If Angel Of Anfield sets a controlled, uncontested lead and the prominent horses track smoothly before kicking from 2f out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pack fails to close sufficiently and Angel Of Anfield, never seriously challenged for the lead, steals enough daylight to hold on.
scenarios.body: If the pack fails to close sufficiently and Angel Of Anfield, never seriously challenged for the lead, steals enough daylight to hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace quickens unexpectedly — perhaps due to multi-horse scrimmaging from the prominent group — burning off enough energy to bring the true hold-up runners into contention.
scenarios.body: If the early pace quickens unexpectedly — perhaps due to multi-horse scrimmaging from the prominent group — burning off enough energy to bring the true hold-up runners into contention.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the middle stages, bunching the field, and multiple horses hit the line together off a slow early gallop.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the middle stages, bunching the field, and multiple horses hit the line together off a slow early gallop.

watchPoints.text: Combustion, Kiniro, and An Outlaw's Grace are all genuine prominent or hold-up horses displaced from their natural positions — if they jostle for ground in the first furlong, they could cause interference and unsettle the early pace pattern significantly.

Desert Cop ran just five days ago and should be monitored in the parade ring and at the start — any sign of a flat or laboured move from the stalls would confirm the quick turnaround has taken a toll before a ball is kicked.

Supreme King's going record (0W0P from 15 on similar ground) is a stark statistic — if he drifts markedly in the market closer to post time it would validate that concern and shift weight toward Marcellinus or Jax Edge as the prominent second-string option.

Star Chorus is fitted with a hood today — watch his demeanour pre-race, as hold-up horses in headgear can occasionally break sharper than expected, and any change in his position off the gates would alter the rear-of-field dynamic meaningfully.

races.name: Sporting Times Sri Lanka Handicap

runners_data.name: Guernsey Lady
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners this David Evans 3yo whose consistent recent form (3rd, 4th, 3rd from five starts) shows she fills places without winning; a genuine hold-up runner who will be racing further forward than ideal given the field's composition, and her similar-going record of just one win from 13 runs on comparable ground gives little extra confidence.

runners_data.name: Eightthreeone
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's 3yo owns a win at 6f on good ground at Goodstock and four placed efforts from seven similar-going starts, making her the most credible of the three runners forced to race closer than their natural game plan; Charles Bishop will look to slot in behind the prominent group and pounce, but the 35-day break is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Adalida
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' yard has had a cold 14-day strike rate (0/19) and this 3yo arrives on the back of a poor run at 11th on good ground, though she does carry a 5f win on good in her history; she prefers to race prominently but will find herself shuffled into midfield with pace ahead, which blunts her chances.

runners_data.name: Quantum Power
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's confirmed front runner and the key pace-setter in this contest: a 5f winner on good ground seven days ago, fitted with a visor, and carried top weight — the fast going and ability to lead uncontested makes his profile the most race-shape-aligned in the field.

runners_data.name: Alkuwarrior
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan rides this hold-up type who won most recently over 5f on soft, making the good-to-firm ground here a mild concern; headgear (p) is applied and the form shows a 14th on good over 6f, though the 5f trip on a flat track is her correct distance when conditions are in her favour.

runners_data.name: Angel Numbers
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator for Dr Richard Newland & Jamie Insole, showing two placings at 5f — one on fast ground and one on standard — but the 7-race form string of 25277 suggests a habitual placing type rather than a winner; Pierre-Louis Jamin gives her a capable pilot and she will appreciate the fast ground if the front side blows up.

runners_data.name: Dark Alley
runners_data.note: Thomas Greatrex (jockey/trainer combination) partners this prominent runner who has a course win at 6f on firm and placed at 5f on good; the 35-day break is the main flag, but his form on fast ground is genuine and he sits just behind Quantum Power as the horse most likely to test the leader if he fires fresh.

runners_data.name: Control Room
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's 3yo has placed twice on soft and won on soft over 5f, which makes the good-to-firm description a mild reservation on going terms; Seamus Cronin (5) claims aboard and the horse holds a recent 2nd on good over 6f, giving him some similar-going credibility, though he looks best suited when conditions are easier.

races.paceDynamic: Quantum Power is the confirmed front runner and, with Billy Loughnane aboard, will stride straight to the lead from the off over this fast Windsor 5f on good-to-firm ground, setting a honest but controllable tempo without any genuine rival capable of matching him stride for stride from the gates. Dark Alley and Control Room are the other natural prominent types who will push forward and occupy the early positions just behind Quantum Power, creating a structured pace that rewards those who travel well close to the action rather than those forced to come from deep. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate at the head of affairs — Eightthreeone, Adalida and Guernsey Lady are all pushed back to a midfield mapping despite their natural instincts, and of those three Eightthreeone is best placed by draw and form to recover closest to her preferred position, while Adalida and Guernsey Lady face the stiffest task racing out of role. The overall shape — a single uncontested leader, honest early fractions, fast ground — strongly favours races settled prominently or just behind the pace, with horses who travel fluidly in the first two to three positions best suited to pounce on the bend into the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Quantum Power Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Quantum Power is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and set a measured, sustainable gallop that his rivals cannot disrupt.
scenarios.body: If Quantum Power is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and set a measured, sustainable gallop that his rivals cannot disrupt.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Peg Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Alley or Control Room applies enough sustained pressure to Quantum Power early that his advantage narrows and the race becomes a sprint finish from 2f out.
scenarios.body: If Dark Alley or Control Room applies enough sustained pressure to Quantum Power early that his advantage narrows and the race becomes a sprint finish from 2f out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than it looks, tying up those at the front and allowing a well-positioned midfield runner to swoop from 1f out.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is stronger than it looks, tying up those at the front and allowing a well-positioned midfield runner to swoop from 1f out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and genuine closers sweep from the rear on fast ground that rewards a long finishing run.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and genuine closers sweep from the rear on fast ground that rewards a long finishing run.

watchPoints.text: Quantum Power (Loughnane) breaks cleanly and sets the fractions — if he crosses to the rail unchallenged inside the first furlong, the race is effectively set up for him to control from the front.

Eightthreeone, Adalida and Guernsey Lady are all competing for positions ahead of their natural style — watch the first two furlongs for congestion if more than one of them pushes forward against the pace.
Dark Alley (35 days off, Thomas Greatrex T&J) is the main threat to Quantum Power if fresh enough — watch how keenly he travels in the early stages as an indicator of his readiness.
Control Room's going form is heavily weighted toward soft/standard — if the track plays quicker than advertised on good-to-firm, his chance of closing late reduces significantly.

Angel Numbers has shown a placed effort at 5f on fast ground, making her the most credible late-closer if the pace scenario unravels, but her win record is absent and she needs a strong pace collapse to threaten.

races.name: Sporting Times Sri Lanka British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Sri Lanka Paradise Island Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Claymore
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who maps as the sole front-runner here for Jane Chapple-Hyam; Billy Loughnane takes over and the horse is rated 94 but recent form reads -27785, suggesting he has dropped well below his best — leads by default rather than merit, and STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence significantly.

runners_data.name: King's Code
runners_data.note: David Evans runner with a checkered recent record (568000) and poor figures on similar going (3/15 sim-going); the hood is fitted and Conor Whiteley claims 5lb, but the overall profile is hard to enthuse about at this trip and on this surface.

runners_data.name: Wisper
runners_data.note: Alan King's eight-year-old recorded a win over 12f on good recently and is a genuine hold-up horse — though the field's density of similar types means he is likely pushed slightly further forward than ideal; Rossa Ryan is a strong booking and the 40-day break is not a concern given that winning run.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Donegal
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old has strong staying form (back-to-back wins at 12f on standard) and Jack Mitchell takes over; naturally wants to race prominently but with Spioradalta and Fireblade also pressing for position, he may be squeezed into a less comfortable spot — visor is fitted and merits respect.

runners_data.name: Thinthread
runners_data.note: French raider from André Fabre off a significant 263-day absence, which is the dominant concern here; naturally races prominently but is likely to find that role crowded, and with no recent racecourse evidence to lean on, the layoff makes assessment very difficult despite the pedigree of the stable.

runners_data.name: Spioradalta
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's six-year-old arrives on a 15-day turnaround and was a winner here on good ground over 10f — the step up to 1m3½f is the key question, but his proven aptitude for this track and sim-going record (4W from 15) give him a strong positional claim just behind Claymore.

runners_data.name: Majestic
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's eight-year-old uses a 5lb claimer in Rose Dawes and is a genuine hold-up type with modest recent form (080-74); best run in similar going came when fourth at 11f, and the step up in trip could help, but the overall profile lacks the finishing kick to win this with confidence.

runners_data.name: Fireblade
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's five-year-old has a clear stamina profile — his wins have come at 16f — so dropping back to 1m3½f is actually a shorter trip than ideal; prominent style should see him positioned well, but Charles Bishop faces the challenge of managing that pace surplus in a race likely to be run at a moderate tempo.

races.paceDynamic: Claymore is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m3½f Windsor circuit on good-to-firm ground. Spioradalta and Fireblade are the next most prominent types and will likely slot in behind Claymore, creating a compact front group but without the pressure to force a genuine test of stamina. Pride Of Donegal, Thinthread, and Wisper are all genuine prominent or hold-up types who cannot all occupy their natural positions — Pride Of Donegal and Spioradalta are best placed to secure the front rank behind Claymore, while Thinthread and Wisper are likely to find themselves further back than ideal. The race shape favours hold-up horses who can produce a strong sustained finish from a fair pace, yet the redistribution of prominent types into midfield means those horses may find traffic or be racing out of role, giving a slight edge to genuine closers capable of picking up ground through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.title: Claymore Controls, Closers Pounce

scenarios.body: If Claymore gets a soft, uncontested lead and the pace is modest enough to set up a one-paced finish.

scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Spioradalta or Pride Of Donegal push the tempo from behind Claymore and the race is run at a genuine clip.
scenarios.body: If Spioradalta or Pride Of Donegal push the tempo from behind Claymore and the race is run at a genuine clip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Burst Wins It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptive and a false rhythm causes a sprint finish off a slow overall time.
scenarios.body: If the pace is deceptive and a false rhythm causes a sprint finish off a slow overall time.

scenarios.title: Front Runner Gallops Clear

watchPoints.text: Wisper is a genuine hold-up horse who won over course-equivalent distance recently — if Rossa Ryan can deliver a clear run from midfield, he is the most dangerous horse in the field given the anticipated moderate pace.

Thinthread's 263-day absence is a major unknown; watch the market move closely — if Fabre has had this race targeted, support would be significant, but any drift should be treated as a serious red flag.

Pride Of Donegal, Thinthread and Wisper are all competing for positions the race shape cannot naturally give them — if they become bunched together in the middle of the field, traffic in the straight could compromise all three simultaneously.

Spioradalta's Windsor course form is the strongest positive angle in the race — a repeat of his recent win here at 10f would require this trip to be within range, so watch how he settles in the early stages as an indicator of whether the step up suits.

Fireblade's optimum trip appears to be beyond today's distance, making this a pace-management puzzle for Charles Bishop — if he is allowed to roll along comfortably from the front group, he could stay on well enough, but a true test of speed at the finish would expose him.

races.name: Visit Sri Lanka Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Hot Silk
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's hold-up filly steps up in trip to 1m3½f which looks well-suited based on her staying pedigree, and the 47-day break could mean she arrives fresh; she has form on similar going and Ross Coakley takes the ride, though from only five runners she will need Glenna to set enough of a gallop to finish past.

runners_data.name: Kindly Queen
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett has solid recent form (6/41 in 14 days) and Rossa Ryan is an upgrade in the saddle — she carries a hood and has placed at 1m4f-1m6f trips, suggesting stamina is not in question; her natural instinct is to come from behind, and with only five runners she may find fewer horses to settle behind than she ideally wants, which tempers confidence in her chance.

runners_data.name: Mohaab
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane rides a filly who won over 10f on soft ground and has strong form credentials on the clock, but her true character as a hold-up horse means a thin field of five creates a positioning puzzle — she will likely find herself closer to the pace than she prefers, and her 0W0P record on good and good-to-firm surfaces is a flag on today's going.

runners_data.name: Glenna
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's 3-year-old is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this race and faces no rivals for the early lead, giving Pierre-Louis Jamin total control of the tempo over a trip she has handled before; her runner-up finish at 12f on soft suggests the step up suits, though her record on good and good-to-firm (2/6, 0W0P) invites some caution about whether the quicker ground will catch her out late.

runners_data.name: Ticker Tape
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's filly has run exclusively on standard (artificial) going in her three career starts, so today's turf on good-to-firm is a completely unknown surface — that is the key unknown here; Robert Havlin's experience is an asset, and she placed third last time at 8f, suggesting the step to 1m3½f could unlock improvement, but the going query cannot be dismissed.

races.paceDynamic: Glenna is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-strong field and faces zero genuine pace rivalry, meaning she can dictate terms from the outset at whatever tempo suits her over this 1m3½f Windsor trip on good-to-firm ground. With no horse likely to challenge her for the lead, Glenna can control the fractions, keep the pace honest but sustainable, and ensure the race is run to her strengths rather than those of the hold-up horses behind her. Hot Silk, Kindly Queen, Mohaab, and Ticker Tape all want to race off the pace, meaning the race will almost certainly be a single-file procession from early on with the chasing pack dependent on Glenna setting them a target to aim at late. The field holds more hold-up types than the shape can naturalistically accommodate at the rear — Kindly Queen and Mohaab are redistributed to midfield on the map but are genuine closers who may genuinely find themselves further back than ideal with so few in the field to tuck behind. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner who can control tempo and a patient closer with strong finishing ability, but the uncontested nature of Glenna's lead makes a front-running or prominent profile the primary tactical beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Glenna — watch whether Pierre-Louis Jamin elects to stride on or dawdle; if she sets a very slow pace the closers will be brought into the race, fundamentally altering the shape.

Ticker Tape — her entire form base is on artificial going and today is her first run on turf; monitor early market moves and paddock demeanour as any sign of greenness or unsettled behaviour would sharply reduce her chance.

Kindly Queen and Mohaab — both are genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map; watch how they jump from the stalls, as a slow break in a five-runner field could leave them trailing with too much ground to find late.

Hot Silk — returning from 47 days off, watch for signs in the paddock or early in the race that she needs the run; James Fanshawe's 3/28 14-day trainer strike rate suggests horses can need a run on return from this yard.
